title: Complete Vertical Scroll Failure Across All Screens and Viewports
reproductionSteps: Navigate to http://127.0.0.1:3099/admin on a display with 1440x900 or 1920x1080 resolution.
Authenticate with admin credentials and open the Projects, Media Library, or Overview tabs.
Attempt to scroll downward using mouse wheel, trackpad, touch swipe, or PageDown / End keys.
Observe that scrollTop remains strictly 0 and all content beyond viewport height (e.g. 1800+ px) is completely unreachable.
actualBehavior: mainScrollH equals mainClientH (e.g. 2605px / 2605px). main does not overflow itself because parent adminRoot and layoutRoot have unconstrained min-h-screen. The entire layout overflows <body>, which has overflow: hidden and height: 100dvh, freezing all vertical movement.
expectedBehavior: The admin root container should be constrained to viewport height (h-[100dvh] overflow-hidden), and the <main> element (or scrollable workspace) should have flex-1 h-full overflow-y-auto so that downward scrolling is natural, responsive, and reaches all content.
rootCause: Global overflow: hidden on html, body in globals.css and layout.tsx combined with min-h-screen on AdminLayout and AdminDashboardClient without a bounded container height or route-scoped overflow configuration.
recommendedFix: In src/app/admin/layout.tsx and AdminDashboardClient.tsx, establish a strict route-scoped container constraint: h-[100dvh] max-h-[100dvh] overflow-hidden on the outer shell, flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto on <main>, and ensure mobile layout allows unified scrolling.
dataImpact: Zero data loss; severe usability blocker preventing access to action buttons, bottom tables, and form inputs.
acceptanceCriteria: On all 7 admin tabs across 1920x1080, 1440x900, 1280x800, 820x1180, 390x844, and 375x812, scrollTop increases on downward wheel/touch/key scroll, and bottom elements are verified reachable via automated Playwright assertions.

title: Interrupted Staging Test Draft Artifact Leaking into Featured Manager
reproductionSteps: Inspect staging D1 projects table via Worker API.
Observe draft project 'staging-e2e-29cbd44d' with featured=1.
Open Featured Manager tab in Admin UI.
Notice that 'Staging E2E Test Projesi' is displayed with button '★ Featured on Desktop'.
actualBehavior: Featured Manager filters projects only by workspace (p.workspace === featuredWorkspace) without checking cmsStatus === 'published'. An uncleaned test draft from an interrupted E2E test appears as featured.
expectedBehavior: Featured Manager should strictly filter for published projects (p.cmsStatus === 'published') or visibly distinguish drafts and prevent unpublished drafts from claiming featured desktop slots.
rootCause: Missing status filter in AdminDashboardClient.tsx lines 1752-1755, and an interrupted run of verify-remote-staging-e2e.mjs that exited prior to its cleanup step.
recommendedFix: Update Featured Manager tab to filter p.cmsStatus === 'published', and add an explicit test cleanup routine or test prefix filter to staging management.
dataImpact: Staging D1 has 31 projects (30 canonical + 1 test draft). Featured count shows 11 instead of 10.
acceptanceCriteria: Featured Manager only renders published projects; test drafts never appear in the desktop featured list; clean inventory documented.

title: Misleading 'Canonical Reconciliation: Pending / MISMATCH' Status
evidenceSource: Admin Overview card and System tab inspection
reproductionSteps: Navigate to Admin Overview tab and observe Cloudflare D1 & R2 card.
Read 'Canonical Reconciliation: Pending'.
Navigate to System tab and read 'Canonical 30-Project Reconciliation: MISMATCH'.
actualBehavior: Because D1 contains 31 projects (the 30 canonical plus 1 draft), nonCanonicalSlugs is not empty, causing reconciled to evaluate to false. Overview displays 'Pending' (fallback for !reconciled) while System displays 'MISMATCH'.
expectedBehavior: Reconciliation logic should differentiate between missing canonical projects (which is an error) vs active drafts created by the administrator (which is normal CMS operation). Overview should say '30/30 Canonical Verified (+ 1 Draft)'.
rootCause: Strict check reconciled = missingSlugs.length === 0 && nonCanonicalSlugs.length === 0 in d1Engine.ts line 1862 treats any draft as a reconciliation failure, and Admin UI conflates false with 'Pending'.
recommendedFix: Refine reconciliation result structure to report canonicalParity: true/false (all 30 canonical projects match) alongside customDraftCount and customProjectCount.
acceptanceCriteria: Overview and System screens accurately reflect 30/30 canonical integrity without displaying a false 'MISMATCH' or 'Pending' when drafts exist.

title: Absence of Manual Desktop Sort Ordering and Drag-and-Drop Placement
reproductionSteps: Open Featured Manager in Admin Dashboard.
Observe that items can only be toggled on or off with 'Set Featured' / '★ Featured on Desktop'.
Attempt to change the order of featured desktop icons.
actualBehavior: No sort order inputs, up/down arrows, or drag-and-drop handles exist. The featuredOrder attribute in D1 cannot be modified from the UI.
expectedBehavior: Administrator should be able to drag-and-drop or use up/down controls / numeric inputs to explicitly specify desktop icon sort order per workspace.
rootCause: Featured Manager was implemented as a simple boolean toggle without ordering UI or endpoint binding for updateFeaturedOrderingInD1.
recommendedFix: Implement a drag-and-drop / Move Up / Move Down list in Featured Manager that updates featured_order in D1 via PUT /api/admin/projects/featured-order.
dataImpact: Prevents curator from controlling the visual hierarchy of desktop icons on https://keremmihci.com.
acceptanceCriteria: Administrator can reorder featured projects; new order persists to D1 and reflects in desktop icon ordering on the public portfolio.

title: Completely Missing 'Videos & Reels' Content Management System
evidenceSource: Inspection of src/data/videos.ts and lack of video management in AdminDashboardClient.tsx
reproductionSteps: Search the admin navigation and interface for video or reel management controls.
Observe that no video management exists anywhere in the CMS dashboard.
Check src/data/videos.ts and observe that all 21 videos (19 portrait reels, 2 landscape videos) are hardcoded in TypeScript.
actualBehavior: All video catalog data, TR/EN titles, descriptions, client metadata, posters, and video paths can only be added or modified by editing TypeScript source code and rebuilding the application.
expectedBehavior: A dedicated 'Videos & Reels' CMS module that allows uploading vertical 9:16 reels and landscape 16:9 videos, editing bilingual metadata, uploading posters, setting sort order, and publishing without code deployment.
rootCause: CMS was initial-phased around project case studies only; standalone video architecture was never migrated into Cloudflare D1/R2.
recommendedFix: Create D1 videos and video_translations tables, add Worker API routes, provide R2 video/poster upload pipeline, and build a dedicated 'Videos & Reels' admin interface.
dataImpact: High; requires non-destructive migration of all 21 existing videos from videos.ts into D1 with zero data loss.
securityImpact: Requires strict video file upload size/MIME validation and streaming support.
acceptanceCriteria: All 21 existing videos editable in CMS; new reels/videos can be uploaded and published dynamically; video files stream correctly via HTTP 206 Range.

title: Session Store Shuffles Video Feed, Overriding Curator Sort Order
reproductionSteps: Open public Portfolio OS and launch VideoApp (Reels).
Refresh the page or open in a new session.
Observe that video order changes randomly on every session initialization.
actualBehavior: const initialVideos = shuffleArray(videosData, createMulberry32(sessionSeed + 1)) shuffles all videos, discarding any intended editorial or chronological order.
expectedBehavior: When the administrator assigns an explicit sort_order, the public Reels feed and Video Library should respect that order deterministically.
rootCause: Hardcoded shuffleArray call on module initialization in sessionStore.ts.
recommendedFix: Update sessionStore.ts to respect explicit sort_order from CMS data, only applying fallback pseudo-randomization if no manual order is specified.
dataImpact: None on database; directly degrades public editorial presentation.
acceptanceCriteria: Curated video order assigned in CMS is strictly preserved across user sessions.

title: Completely Missing 'Personal Gallery' Content Management System
evidenceSource: Inspection of src/data/gallery.ts (empty array) and AdminDashboardClient.tsx
reproductionSteps: Inspect public GalleryApp.tsx (Photos app on Portfolio OS desktop).
Observe that it shows an empty state because galleryItems in gallery.ts is empty ([]).
Search admin dashboard for personal gallery management controls.
Observe that no module exists to publish photos to the personal gallery.
actualBehavior: Personal Gallery cannot be populated or managed through the CMS. It is completely disconnected from the existing project_media table.
expectedBehavior: A dedicated 'Personal Gallery' CMS module allowing photo uploads, selection from R2 library, caption/year/location editing, single-column feed preview, and manual top-to-bottom reordering.
rootCause: Personal gallery was never integrated into D1/R2; project_media table is strictly bound to project case studies.
recommendedFix: Create D1 personal_gallery table with sort_order, captions, and R2 bindings; build a specialized vertical feed curator in the admin dashboard.
dataImpact: High content capability addition; public GalleryApp moves from empty placeholder to live photostream.
acceptanceCriteria: Administrator can upload photos, arrange their vertical feed sequence, and publish to the public GalleryApp with immediate live availability.

title: Session Store Randomly Shuffles Gallery Feed on Session Initialization
reproductionSteps: Inspect src/store/sessionStore.ts line 63.
Observe initialGallery = shuffleArray(galleryItems, createMulberry32(sessionSeed + 2)).
actualBehavior: Any gallery images added to sessionGallery are shuffled using a random session seed.
expectedBehavior: Personal gallery must display as a deliberate, sequential, single-column top-to-bottom feed as requested by the user, respecting manual curator sort order.
recommendedFix: Sort gallery items by sort_order ascending without shuffling.
acceptanceCriteria: Public GalleryApp displays images in exact manual sort order configured in the CMS.

title: Static Profile Content (Biography, Experience, Education, Skills, Notes) Uneditable via CMS
reproductionSteps: Attempt to update biography, career history, education, skills, or personal notes in the administration dashboard.
Observe that no editing interfaces exist for any of these sections.
actualBehavior: All six sections of the NotesApp are hardcoded in src/data/profile.ts and cannot be updated without code modification and production build.
expectedBehavior: Dedicated 'Profile & CV' and 'Notes' modules in the admin dashboard allowing full bilingual CRUD for biography, stats, career history, education, skill badges, and written notes.
rootCause: Profile data model was never migrated to D1.
recommendedFix: Create D1 tables for profile, profile_translations, experience_items, education_items, skills, and notes; build structured CMS management forms with live preview.
dataImpact: Requires non-destructive migration of all profileData records from profile.ts into D1.
securityImpact: Content sanitization (HTML/script injection prevention in notes text).
acceptanceCriteria: All 6 tabs of NotesApp dynamically load from D1; administrator can update profile and notes without rebuild.

title: CV PDFs Unavailable and Cannot Be Uploaded or Managed via CMS
reproductionSteps: Inspect public/cv/ directory. Observe that it contains zero files.
Inspect profile.ts: cv.trAvailable = false and cv.enAvailable = false.
Search admin dashboard for CV upload controls. Observe none exist.
actualBehavior: Public CV downloads are marked unavailable because no PDF files exist on disk, and there is no administrative tool to upload or replace CVs.
expectedBehavior: Administrator can upload Turkish and English CV PDF documents, inspect current versions, toggle public availability, preview files, and replace them without code edits.
rootCause: Lack of document upload pipeline in Worker/CMS and missing PDF assets.
recommendedFix: Add secure PDF document upload endpoint to Worker (with application/pdf magic-byte signature check and size limits), store in R2 at documents/cv/..., and provide a dedicated CV management card in Profile CMS.
dataImpact: Eliminates broken/unavailable CV links on the public site.
securityImpact: Strict PDF MIME and magic byte verification required to prevent arbitrary document upload.
acceptanceCriteria: Administrator can upload and replace TR and EN CV PDFs; public CvApp and NotesCvTab reflect active download links.

title: Missing Unsaved Changes Protection (Dirty State Tracking)
reproductionSteps: Open Project Editor and make extensive edits to title, descriptions, or deliverables.
Accidentally click another sidebar tab (e.g. Media Library or Overview) or refresh/close the browser tab.
Return to Editor. Observe that all modifications are permanently discarded with zero warning.
actualBehavior: Component switches activeTab immediately without checking if formState is dirty, causing immediate data loss of uncommitted work.
expectedBehavior: Persistent dirty state indicator ('Unsaved Changes'); confirmation dialog before tab navigation or page unload ('You have unsaved changes. Discard?').
rootCause: No isDirty state comparison between formState and initial project data, and no window.addEventListener('beforeunload') guard.
recommendedFix: Implement useMemo isDirty check, add beforeunload listener, and add an in-app confirmation modal when switching tabs with unsaved edits.
dataImpact: High administrative risk of lost editorial work.
acceptanceCriteria: Administrator is alerted before leaving an edited form with unsaved changes; beforeunload blocks accidental tab closure.

title: Raw String URL Inputs Without Visual Thumbnail Previews in Editor
reproductionSteps: Open Project Editor.
Scroll to Cover, Thumbnail, and Gallery Media sections.
Observe that media items are displayed as plain text inputs containing storage paths (e.g. /projects/slug/cover/...) with no visual image preview.
actualBehavior: Administrator must inspect raw text URLs without visual confirmation of which image is assigned as cover, thumbnail, or gallery items.
expectedBehavior: Rich media preview cards showing image thumbnails, dimensions, replace button, and visual drag-and-drop ordering.
rootCause: Minimalist text input implementation in AdminDashboardClient.tsx.
recommendedFix: Upgrade Project Media section to visual cards displaying image previews with quick-replace, remove, and alt-text popovers.
acceptanceCriteria: Every assigned project media item renders a crisp thumbnail preview with clear management controls.

title: Media Library Lacks Asset Deletion, Search, Filtering, and One-Click URL Copy
reproductionSteps: Navigate to Media Library tab.
Attempt to search for an asset by filename or filter by type (image vs video).
Attempt to copy the public URL of an asset with one click.
Attempt to delete an unused or test media file from R2.
actualBehavior: Grid renders only the first 60 assets statically without search input, filter pills, copy URL button, or deletion action.
expectedBehavior: Search bar, filter by project/type, one-click 'Copy URL' toast, asset inspector modal with file size/dimensions, and safe delete button with orphan checking.
rootCause: Media Library was implemented as a simple gallery grid without interactive asset management actions.
recommendedFix: Add search/filter controls, clipboard API integration, asset inspector drawer, and safe delete flow via DELETE /api/admin/media.
dataImpact: Low; enables cleanup of orphan media in R2.
securityImpact: Deletion must ensure no published project references the deleted media key.
acceptanceCriteria: Administrator can search assets, copy URLs to clipboard, view metadata, and safely delete orphan R2 files.

title: Monolithic 1,900+ Line Single-File Client Component (AdminDashboardClient.tsx)
reproductionSteps: Inspect src/app/admin/AdminDashboardClient.tsx.
Observe 1,909 lines of code containing login, overview, project list, editor, media, featured, system, and settings in a single component.
actualBehavior: All state (projects, media, system, formState, filters, login) lives in one monolithic component, causing unnecessary re-renders across tabs and high maintenance complexity.
expectedBehavior: Modular tab architecture with dedicated subcomponents (OverviewTab, ProjectsTab, ProjectEditorTab, MediaTab, FeaturedTab, SystemTab, SettingsTab) and shared context or custom hooks.
rootCause: Rapid prototype consolidation during initial CMS hardening.
recommendedFix: Refactor AdminDashboardClient into clean modular subcomponents under src/components/admin/ during Phase 2 design system modernization.
acceptanceCriteria: AdminDashboardClient decomposed into modular subcomponents; test coverage and type check remain 100% green.

title: Large Video Upload Request Size Constraints Through Next.js Proxy
evidenceSource: Next.js API route body parser limits & Cloudflare Worker 100MB body limit
reproductionSteps: Attempt to upload a high-bitrate video file (e.g. 150MB - 500MB) through /api/admin/media.
Observe failure due to proxy payload limits or gateway timeouts.
actualBehavior: Current media upload passes file buffers through Next.js server route to Cloudflare Worker. Cloudflare Worker standard body limits (100MB) and Next.js body parser limits will reject large video uploads.
expectedBehavior: Optimized video upload flow: either presigned direct R2 upload URLs or validated client-side multipart chunking for large video files, with progress bar.
rootCause: Upload architecture was designed for small WebP images (<10MB), not high-definition video files.
recommendedFix: Implement direct authenticated R2 presigned PUT URLs or direct Worker multipart upload for video assets exceeding 50MB, with client-side upload progress indication.
dataImpact: Prevents failed or corrupted video uploads.
securityImpact: Presigned URLs must have short TTL (e.g. 15 minutes) and validate authorized session.
acceptanceCriteria: Videos up to 250MB upload reliably with real-time percentage progress bar and R2 storage confirmation.
